speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) how many students are graduating from studies in hospitality, aviation and aerospace in 2021; and (b) whether and how will the Government support these graduating students to gain meaningful employment engagements given the challenges faced by these sectors during the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: The hospitality, aviation and aerospace sectors have been particularly impacted.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Graduates also receive career guidance and assistance through the IHL Career Centres, WSG's Career Connect Centres and NTUC's e2i career centres.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Graduates from harder-hit sectors, such as hospitality, aviation and aerospace, who wish to explore new opportunities in adjacent sectors can also access career fairs organised by the IHLs as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Graduates from the Class of 2020 and 2021 can also tap on the free Continuing Education and Training modules offered by the IHLs to enhance their skills while they seek employment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: These courses will be available until March 2022.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: These measures have helped cushion the impact of a challenging job market.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister Shanmugam, I think you have something to raise?
